snippet.title: What IRAN Looked Like 2,500 Years Ago Before It Burned (AI Reconstruction)
snippet.description:
Basically, in this video, I use AI to "resurrect" Persepolis—located in modern-day Iran —or Parsa, as the Persians called it , and step into its grand halls exactly as they were around 450 BC, right before its spectacular downfall. It’s not just about looking at buildings; we explore the massive artificial platform , the Gate of All Nations guarded by colossal stone bulls , and the magnificent Apadana audience hall at their absolute peak. We contrast that vibrant reality—where twenty-three different nations gathered during the Nowruz spring festival to share feasts and exchange tribute —with the scorched, silent ruins that remain today.

We also break down the exact night Alexander the Great arrived , and how a chaotic victory feast led an Athenian companion named Thaïs to throw the torch that burned two hundred years of construction to the ground. It’s crazy to see what was actually lost in the ashes, especially since archaeological payroll records prove this monumental city was built entirely by free, compensated workers across ethnic lines, not slaves.

snippet.title: What Los Angeles Really Looked Like in 1900 (AI Reconstruction)
snippet.description:
Basically, in this video, I use AI to bring Los Angeles back to life exactly as it rose between 1876 and 1920 — from a dusty Mexican pueblo with no harbor, no reliable river, and no reason to exist, into the fastest-growing city in America. It's not just about looking at buildings; we walk the adobe plaza of the old pueblo, the orange groves that once carpeted the basin, and the forest of oil derricks that sprouted up between people's houses. We contrast that improbable, hand-built reality with the endless modern metropolis that eventually swallowed it whole.

We also break down exactly how a town with nothing talked itself into existence — from selling its own sunshine as medicine and the one-dollar train ticket that flooded the West, to the seven-year war for a harbor carved out of a mudflat, and the moment William Mulholland reached 230 miles north, took an entire river, and turned to the crowd to say five words the city would never forget: "There it is. Take it." It's crazy to see how a place that should never have existed manufactured everything it needed — and then invented the one thing no geography can grant or deny: Hollywood, the dream itself.

00:54 Los Angeles 1876
03:06 Los Angeles 1886 - Selling the Sunshine 
06:34 Los Angeles 1899 -  A Harbor Carved From Mud
10:46 Los Angeles 1900
15:22 Los Angeles 1910

snippet.title: What Rome Looked Like at the Height of the Roman Empire (AI Reconstruction)
snippet.description:
Basically, in this video, I use modern AI to reconstruct Rome at its absolute peak. We're going to walk its streets and witness how one million people lived in humanity's first truly modern city during the Pax Romana (27 BC - 180 AD). It’s not just about looking at monuments; we explore the towering apartment buildings where 90% of Romans lived, the massive public baths that acted as the ultimate social equalizer, and the sheer spectacle of the Colosseum.

We also break down the unexpected tragedy of this era: how the golden age eventually began to collapse under the watch of the philosopher-emperor Marcus Aurelius, battling plague and invasions while writing his famous Meditations. It’s crazy to see how a city built for eternity transitioned from gold to rust.

📚 If you enjoyed the video and want to expand your knowledge about Rome, I highly recommend these books:

snippet.title: What Chicago Really Looked Like in 1893 (AI Reconstruction)
snippet.description:
Basically, in this video, I use AI to "resurrect" the legendary White City — the 1893 World's Fair raised on the shore of Lake Michigan — and walk its gleaming streets exactly as they were that one unforgettable summer. It's not just about looking at buildings; we explore the two hundred white palaces, the colossal Ferris Wheel that lifted more than two thousand people into the sky, and the staggering display of electric light that ran on the alternating current championed by Tesla and Westinghouse. We contrast that dazzling reality — where close to half of America came to glimpse the future — with the empty stretch of lakefront grass that is almost all that remains today.

We also break down the incredible story behind it: how a city that had burned to ashes in the Great Fire of 1871 rebuilt itself, invented the skyscraper, and then raised an entire dream-city out of a drowned marsh in barely two years — only to watch fire claim the White City all over again. It's crazy to see what was actually lost, especially since the whole magnificent metropolis was never marble at all, but plaster and paint built to shine for a single season.

00:45 Chicago 1871 - The City That Burned
03:12 Chicago 1890 - The City That Learned to Touch the Sky
06:57 Chicago 1893 - Building the Impossible
11:12 Chicago 1893 - The White City
14:41 Chicago 1894 - The City That Vanished

snippet.title: London 1300: The Apocalypse Happened in 1348 (AI Reconstruction)
snippet.description:
In this video! I’m taking you straight back to London in the year 1300, when it was at its medieval peak with 100,000 people.

I’ve used AI to reconstruct what life was actually like there. You’ll see the Old St. Paul’s Cathedral, which was way taller than the one standing today , and the London Bridge, which wasn't just a bridge—it was a floating city with over 140 buildings hanging over the water.

But the most intense part is seeing how this massive city almost hit the end of the world. I explain how they faced three years of nonstop rain that caused a brutal famine , and then the Black Death, which killed about 6 out of every 10 Londoners in just a few months.

It’s crazy to see how the survivors managed to change the social order and rebuild everything from the ruins. Check it out and let me know which era I should reconstruct next!

snippet.title: What Carthage ACTUALLY Looked Like Before Rome Burned It (AI Reconstruction)
snippet.description:
Basically, in this video, I use AI to "resurrect" Carthage—located in modern-day Tunisia—or Qart Hadasht, as the Phoenicians called it, and walk its streets exactly as they were around 150 BC, right before its total annihilation. It's not just about looking at buildings; we explore the secret circular military harbor that hid two hundred and twenty warships, the triple walls with three hundred war elephants living inside their base, and the bustling markets of the wealthiest city in the Western Mediterranean at their absolute peak. We contrast that vibrant reality—where merchants from dozens of nations traded in Phoenician, Greek, and a dozen other languages—with the ash and foundation stones that remain today.

We also break down the exact six days of apocalyptic urban combat that erased a seven-hundred-year-old civilization, and how a Roman senator's obsession—Carthago delenda est—turned a commercial rival into a ghost. It's crazy to see what was actually lost in those flames, especially since Rome then quietly adopted Carthage's farming techniques, its iconic fruit, and the very sword design that built the Roman Empire.

snippet.title: What Jerusalem Actually Looked Like Before Rome Destroyed It (AI Reconstruction)
snippet.description:
Basically, in this video, we bring Jerusalem back to life at its absolute peak, mere moments before it was consumed by fire and lost to time. It’s not just about looking at buildings; we explore the massive 36-acre Temple Mount that Herod the Great built , walking through the bustling Court of the Gentiles , and contrasting the palatial mansions of the Upper City with the crowded, noisy streets of the Lower City.

We also break down the exact events that led to the city's tragic fate, from the rise of early extremist factions like the Sicarii to the catastrophic siege by Roman forces in 70 AD. It’s crazy to see the historical irony of what was lost, and how Rome actually used the looted gold and enslaved population from Jerusalem's destruction to finance and build the Colosseum.

snippet.title: Tenochtitlan 1519: The Greatest City the Spanish Had Ever Seen  (AI Reconstruction)
snippet.description:
In this video! I’m taking you straight to Tenochtitlan in the year 1519, the "Venice of the Americas" and one of the largest cities in the world at its peak.

I’ve used AI tools to bring this extraordinary metropolis back to life, from the sacred Templo Mayor rising 60 meters over the city to the massive market of Tlatelolco, which was so grand it astonished the Spanish conquistadors. You’ll see how the Mexica mastered the water with a complex system of canals and chinampas—artificial islands that could yield up to seven harvests a year to feed hundreds of thousands.

But the most intense part is witnessing how this invincible city was reduced to ruins in just months during the Spanish siege. I’ll also show you what remains today, literally buried beneath the streets and buildings of modern Mexico City.

It’s a journey that shows what human ingenuity can achieve in the middle of a swamp. Check it out and let me know in the comments what other lost city I should revive next!

snippet.title: What Kyoto ACTUALLY Looked Like After It Burned (AI Reconstruction)
snippet.description:
Basically, in this video, I use AI to "resurrect" Kyoto—located in medieval Japan—exactly as it was in 1461, right before and during its catastrophic decade of destruction. It's not just about looking at temples; we explore the city at its most broken: a capital where 82,000 corpses dammed the Kamo River, while the shogun inside his palace hosted poetry competitions. We contrast that violent, chaotic reality with the stunning cultural legacy that emerged from those same ashes.

We also break down the exact political collapse that triggered the Onin War—how a succession dispute between two warlords sent a quarter million soldiers into a city built of wood, paper, and straw—and how the commoners who survived invented Japan's first form of civil self-government. It's crazy to see how everything the world calls "Japanese culture" — the tea ceremony, zen gardens, wabi-sabi, kintsugi — was born directly from a city that lost 80% of everything it had ever built.

snippet.title: The 7 Wonders Before Time Destroyed Them (AI Reconstruction)
snippet.description:
In this video! I’m taking you on the definitive "Grand Tour" of antiquity to discover the 7 Wonders of the World as they’ve never been seen before.

I’ve used modern AI tools to bring these legendary sites back to life, from historical descriptions and archaeological ruins. You’ll see the Great Pyramid of Giza covered in polished white limestone that looks like solid light , and the Hanging Gardens of Babylon, a green hallucination in the desert with artificial waterfalls. We even go inside the Temple of Zeus to see a 12-meter statue of gold and ivory that was so large it almost touched the ceiling.

But the coolest part is that we don't just stay in the past. I’ll take you to those same locations today to see what survived the earthquakes, fires, and looting over the last two thousand years. It’s fascinating to see how a mountain of marble like the Mausoleum at Halicarnassus ended up as part of a medieval castle.

It’s a journey that proves human ambition has no limits. Check it out and let me know in the comments which lost city or historical moment I should revive next!

06:04 Temple of Artemis at Ephesus
07:35 Mausoleum at Halicarnassus

snippet.title: What Tombstone Really Looked Like in 1881 (AI Reconstruction)
snippet.description:
Most people know Tombstone because of the famous gunfight at the O.K. Corral. Almost nobody knows how the city itself actually died.
In this AI reconstruction, we travel back to Tombstone at the height of its power, when a silver strike turned a barren stretch of Arizona desert into one of the richest and most surprising cities in the American West. We'll walk its crowded streets, visit its theaters, saloons, and luxury restaurants, and discover how a town with no water managed to become a booming metropolis almost overnight.

snippet.title: Machu Picchu 1500: The IMPOSSIBLE City in the Clouds (AI Reconstruction)
snippet.description:
In this video! I’m taking you straight back to the Andes Mountains in the year 1450, where the clouds meet the stone at 2,430 meters high. 

I’ve used AI to reconstruct Machu Picchu at its absolute peak. You’ll see how they carved a city from living rock without iron tools or wheels, fitting granite blocks so perfectly a knife blade can't slide between them, and a hydraulic system so advanced it still works 500 years later. 

But the most intense part is discovering why they abandoned this masterpiece barely a century after finishing it. I explain how they burned the forest trails behind them to hide it from Spanish invaders, allowing it to vanish into legend for 371 years. 

It’s crazy to see how the engineering allowed it to withstand centuries of earthquakes while modern buildings crumbled. Check it out and let me know which ancient wonder I should reconstruct next!

snippet.title: Angkor Wat: The Lost Megacity Hidden in the Jungle (AI Reconstruction)
snippet.description:
Basically, in this video, I use modern AI to reconstruct Angkor Wat at its absolute peak—before the droughts, floods, and its eventual collapse. We travel back to the year 1296 to walk through the world's greatest hydraulic city, exactly as it was. It’s not just about looking at buildings; we explore the daily life of its 750,000 inhabitants through the accounts of Zhou Daguan, the only surviving first-person eyewitness to document it. We contrast that vibrant reality—central towers blazing with gold leaf and bustling markets run entirely by female merchants—with the silent, jungle-swallowed ruins revealed by modern LIDAR technology today.

We also break down the exact moment the climate turned chaotic, bringing decades of severe drought followed by extreme monsoons. It’s crazy to see how the very water and sophisticated engineering system that sustained this massive pre-industrial civilization for 500 years ultimately destroyed it.

snippet.title: What Constantinople ACTUALLY Looked Like Before the Sun Went Dark (AI Reconstruction)
snippet.description:
Basically, in this video, I use AI to reconstruct Constantinople at its absolute peak—a metropolis of half a million people, the most advanced city on Earth, while the rest of Europe was collapsing into darkness. It's not just about looking at buildings; we explore the indestructible Theodosian Walls, the underground Basilica Cistern held up by 336 columns, and the impossible dome of Hagia Sophia at their absolute peak. We contrast that vibrant reality—where a peasant emperor and a former actress rewrote the laws of the entire Western world—with the silent ruins and sunken legends that remain today.

We also break down the exact moment the city tore itself apart during the Nika Revolt, how Theodora's single speech saved an empire, and how two monks hid silkworm eggs inside bamboo walking sticks to pull off the most daring act of industrial espionage in history. It's crazy to see what was actually built on the ashes of that chaos, especially since the legal code Justinian commissioned still governs France, Germany, Japan, and most of Latin America today.

snippet.title: Walking through Athens 2,500 years ago (AI Reconstruction)
snippet.description:
Basically, in this video, we reconstruct the most extraordinary eighty years in the life of Athens. We explore how the city rose from a burnt-out shell left by the Persians to become the greatest naval empire the ancient Mediterranean had ever seen. It's not just about looking at pristine white marble; we explore how a cracked, cruel, brilliant democracy built the Parthenon using allied defense money , contrasting the violent blues, blood reds, and sweating marble gods of the Acropolis with the hellish reality of the Laurium silver mines. Down there, thousands of slaves were worked to a waxy death in oven-like temperatures to fund the empire's reserve currency. 

We also break down the terrifying machine of Athenian justice , the devastating plague that wiped out a third of the city's population , and how the citizens voted, one assembly at a time, to hand their city over to its enemies. It's crazy to see how the same people who built a wooden wall of ships to save Western civilization ultimately built a wall of fear high enough to execute their own victorious generals , vote to massacre neutral islands like Melos , and force Socrates to drink hemlock. Sparta didn't conquer Athens; Athens conquered itself.

snippet.title: What Medieval Kyiv Looked Like 1,000 Years Ago Before History Forgot It (AI Reconstruction)
snippet.description:
Basically, in this video, I use AI to "resurrect" Kyiv — the Viking capital of the Slavic world — and walk its streets exactly as they were around 1050 AD, right before the empire it built began to fracture from within. It's not just about looking at buildings; we explore the massive slave-trading docks of the Podol, the golden domes of Saint Sophia rising above the Dnieper, and the ceremonial Golden Gate at the absolute peak of their power. We contrast that extraordinary reality — where a Slavic-Viking-Byzantine hybrid ruled more territory than the Holy Roman Empire — with the fragments and ruins that survive today.

We also break down the exact moment a young warlord returned from exile, drowned his own pagan gods in a river, and built a Christian empire in a single generation. It's crazy to see what was actually lost to history, especially since a Kievan princess signed her name in Cyrillic on a French throne — decades before the Normans ever crossed the Channel.

snippet.title: Knossos 1700 BC: Europe's First Civilization (AI Reconstruction)
snippet.description:
In this video! I’m taking you straight back to the island of Crete in the year 1700 BC, where Europe’s very first civilization is reaching its absolute peak.

I’ve used AI to reconstruct the legendary Palace of Knossos. You’ll see a massive complex of over 1,000 rooms with no fortification walls , featuring a plumbing system with flushing toilets that wouldn't be matched in Europe for another 3,000 years.


But the most intense part is seeing how this society was completely different from anything else in history. I explain how this was a civilization ruled not by kings, but by high priestesses , and how they faced two apocalyptic catastrophes: a volcanic explosion with the force of millions of atomic bombs , followed by an invasion of warriors from mainland Greece.


It’s crazy to see how this peaceful, goddess-worshiping culture was transformed into the myths of the Labyrinth and the Minotaur. Check it out and let me know which lost civilization I should reconstruct next!

snippet.title: Birmingham 1900: The City That Promised Paradise
snippet.description:
Basically, in this video, I use AI to "resurrect" Birmingham—the red-brick city that armed the British Empire—and walk its streets exactly as they were between 1890 and 1929, at the absolute peak of its industrial power. It's not just about looking at factories; we explore the Jewellery Quarter where seventy thousand craftsmen made more than half the jewelry in the entire Empire, the BSA arms works that produced 1.5 million rifles for a single war, and the monumental Council House of a city that declared itself the best-governed on earth—at their absolute peak. We contrast that vibrant reality—the cleanest mountain water on the British mainland, the first municipal bank in the country, the oldest cinema still standing in Britain—with the one hundred and eight thousand toxic back-to-back houses where its workers slept under the same yellow smoke that built the Empire.

We also break down the real story the world never got right: who the actual Peaky Blinders were—teenage boys with belt buckles and bad luck, not razor blades sewn into caps—how the most liberal democracy on earth built an industrial torture system inside its own model prison to force-feed women asking to vote, and how Birmingham armed an entire world war while sending its own sons to die with the weapons their wives and mothers had just forged. It's crazy to see what this city sacrificed to keep an empire running, especially since—unlike every other lost city we've rebuilt on this channel, destroyed by fire, water, armies, or plague—Birmingham was suffocated by the one thing it refused to admit: the same red brick that built the Empire was choking the people inside it.

snippet.title: What San Francisco Really Looked Like in 1906 (AI Reconstruction)
snippet.description:
Basically, in this video, I use AI to "resurrect" San Francisco and walk its streets exactly as they were on the morning of April 18th, 1906 — the richest young city in America, just hours before it was lost. It's not just about looking at buildings; we explore the Palace Hotel, the wooden palaces of Nob Hill, the towering Call Building and the lantern-lit alleys of Chinatown at their absolute peak, contrasting that vibrant reality — the "Paris of the West," a city of wood and gold raised in a single lifetime — with the smoking ruins that remained just three days later.

We also break down the cruelest twist of the whole disaster: how a city completely ringed by water burned to the ground because it had nothing left to drink. snippet.title: What Edinburgh ACTUALLY Looked Like Before the Great Invasion of 1544 (AI Reconstruction)
snippet.description:
Basically, in this video, we travel back to the year 1544 to walk the streets of medieval Edinburgh right before it faced the largest invasion force Edinburg - Scotland had seen in a generation. It’s not just about looking at a fortress; we explore life in the densely packed Royal Mile, where timber buildings leaned so far over that neighbors could shake hands from their windows. We contrast that vibrant reality—including its groundbreaking medical anatomy theaters, revolutionary printing presses, and experimental artillery hidden in narrow closes —with the devastating reality of the "Rough Wooing".

We also break down the exact timeline of King Henry VIII's naval arrival and how an army acting on brutally simple orders buried a city in fire for three continuous days. It’s crazy to see how the ashes of this medieval town, which looked at total destruction and chose defiance, eventually paved the way for the Scottish Enlightenment.

snippet.title: Pompeii: Before the Disaster (AI Reconstruction)
snippet.description:
Basically, in this video, I use AI to "resurrect" Pompeii and walk its streets exactly as they were in 79 AD, right before the disaster. It’s not just about looking at buildings; we explore life in the Forum, the Temples, and the Villa of the Mysteries at their peak, contrasting that vibrant reality (the colors, the people, the intact architecture) with the silent ruins that remain today.

We also break down the exact moment Vesuvius woke up and how that "mountain," which everyone thought was harmless, buried an entire city in a matter of hours. It’s crazy to see what was actually lost beneath the ash.

01:14 The Early City: The humble origins of the Forum (4th Century BC).
02:02 The Forum in 79 AD: The civic heart of the city & ongoing repairs.
03:31 Temple of Jupiter: Roman authority under the shadow of Vesuvius.

05:54 The Basilica: Justice and business in the courthouse.
07:06 Walking the Streets: Daily life, shops, and graffiti.
08:01 The Amphitheater: Gladiators and entertainment.
09:00 Villa of the Mysteries: Luxury and secret rituals outside the walls.
10:20 The Eruption (1:00 PM): Vesuvius explodes and burying the city.
12:33 The Aftermath: Rediscovery and the "time capsule" effect.
14:16 Pompeii Today: Comparing the ruins (Forum, Temples, Basilica) to the past.
